mbm-2901.clue: My notebook has a spare front door.
mbm-2901.quote: I start a story from the front and write its ending from the back. When the pages meet, I give the characters a front door they can both reach. The last one was painted a ridiculous purple.

mbm-2902.clue: The little dock ladder earned a medal.
mbm-2902.quote: I fell off my skis ten times learning to cross the wake. The ladder hauled me out for ten more tries. I tied a scrap of red ribbon to the top rung after my first clean crossing.

mbm-2903.clue: Our skis have jaws but no teeth.
mbm-2903.quote: My dad built a little rack shaped like a V for our water skis. Spread the bright red tips apart and they look like a fish opening its mouth. My nephew feeds it pebbles when nobody's looking.

mbm-2904.clue: The tiny mechanic wears my grandfather's apron.
mbm-2904.quote: Grandpa gave me a scrap of faded blue cotton for my model pilot's suit. I made a pocket too. You need a magnifier to see the little red screwdriver peeking out of it.

mbm-2905.clue: I send my calls from a crooked chair.
mbm-2905.quote: One leg of my radio chair is short. I put my first thick logbook under it. All those old signals are doing a fine job keeping the new ones steady.

mbm-2906.clue: I know which chapter the thunderclap belongs to.
mbm-2906.quote: I was writing a quarrel when thunder rattled the pencil cup. I turned the quarrel into a scene where both people stop to shut the same window. The storm fixed my story better than a whole evening of crossing words out.

mbm-2907.clue: I learned my best trick with a baked potato.
mbm-2907.quote: I practiced juggling against the garden wall till an early potato bounced into my mum's apron. She handed it back wearing a paper crown. The king always gets the last catch now.

mbm-2908.clue: Nobody on our boat can draw a straight banana.
mbm-2908.quote: We take a banana on every water-ski outing. After your final run you draw the shape of your turns on its peel. At lunch Dad cuts it into equal shares and passes round the day's best figure eight.

mbm-2909.clue: My first audience was a roomful of coats.
mbm-2909.quote: I practiced singing in the cloakroom before the school concert. The winter coats swallowed all the echo. My father still calls a quiet rehearsal singing to the overcoats.

mbm-2910.clue: I sing the gap in the record.
mbm-2910.quote: My mum's old record has a worn spot where the singer drops out for a beat. I fill the gap with her favorite word. Now the clean recording always sounds one word short to me.

mbm-2911.clue: The best thing I lifted that winter was a stool.
mbm-2911.quote: I kept my workout log on the floor until our gym caretaker gave me a little stool he'd fixed. Now everybody leaves their log on it. By closing time there's a tower of notebooks and one careful hand lifting each person's day off the top.

mbm-2912.clue: I keep a second button on my cuff.
mbm-2912.quote: I sewed a spare shell button below the proper one on my travel shirt. At the bus station I used it to fix a stranger's jacket. I stitched another spare on when I got home.

mbm-2913.clue: I saved the note the wind took away.
mbm-2913.quote: In our outdoor concert a gust flipped the last page of my music. The crowd sang the missing line back to me. I found the page under a chair later and framed it with a little piece of grass.

mbm-2914.clue: My frisbee takes the scenic route.
mbm-2914.quote: At family picnics we try to float the disc round the end of the long table and back to the thrower. My aunt once caught it with one hand and never put down her lemonade. We retired that record.

mbm-2915.clue: I can still hear the bench come apart.
mbm-2915.quote: Halfway through our son set, a slat slipped off the bench where my cousins sat. They finished the tune standing up. I kept the slat, sanded it smooth and made two sets of practice claves so they could take the rhythm home.

mbm-2916.clue: My paddle knows which side gets the sunrise.
mbm-2916.quote: One blade of my old kayak paddle faded in the boat shed window. At dawn I put the pale blade toward the light. My partner can spot me from the next cove.

mbm-2917.clue: The pocket hangs at a dancing angle.
mbm-2917.quote: I sewed a pocket on crooked because I was listening to a quick record. It holds my hand perfectly when I dance. I put the second pocket on to match the music.

mbm-2918.clue: I saved my grandpa's two useful inches.
mbm-2918.quote: Grandpa never threw away a cloth scrap wider than two fingers. I joined his little pieces into a long striped quilt border. It goes round our biggest bed and back to the first stripe.

mbm-2919.clue: Someone planted corn in my geometric quilt.
mbm-2919.quote: My cousin turned four yellow diamonds on their sides and gave them green embroidered leaves. When I spread out the finished blanket she kneels in the middle to check her crop.

mbm-2920.clue: My patchwork rainbow has a brown stripe.
mbm-2920.quote: We used old school uniforms for most of it. The brown stripe is from the bus driver's spare jacket. My classmates all agreed he was part of getting us over the rainbow.

mbm-2921.clue: The rope makes a rainbow for one second.
mbm-2921.quote: After a clean water-ski turn the tow rope shakes off little drops. With the sun behind me a rainbow runs along it toward the boat. I keep both hands steady and watch it go.

mbm-2922.clue: I made the castle from a piano box.
mbm-2922.quote: Our theater needed a castle tower and the music shop had a tall empty crate. I painted the old delivery label as a little balcony. The princess leaned out of a place that once held a piano leg.

mbm-2923.clue: My queen has a sewn-on crown.
mbm-2923.quote: I keep the park chess set in an old drawstring sack. One queen lost her finial, so I stitched a tiny felt crown to it. My opponents take care not to squish her when they shake hands.

mbm-2924.clue: Our boat had very particular table manners.
mbm-2924.quote: The guide told us to keep our little snack box sealed before the next stretch of rapids. We did. At lunch we opened it to find all eight sandwiches lined up on their ends. I drew the little family portrait before anyone took a bite.

mbm-2925.clue: I know a canoe can carry a whole moon.
mbm-2925.quote: My brother and I paddled back to the dock after sunset. Every time we lifted a paddle the moon broke apart on the water, then pieced itself together between strokes. We took our time getting home.
